## Review result

No candidate-caused blocking security or privacy defect was admitted. The deadline-classification defects exposed after the R5 review are repaired without weakening cancellation precedence, secure-target rejection, the application-bound ordinary-miss exception, or any previously closed output boundary.

## Explicit AX deadline and cancellation propagation

- The concrete System runtime now preserves cancellation and deadline as distinct typed cases throughout element, string, settable, range, PID, operation, checkpoint, and editable assessments (`FeishuSpeech/Services/AccessibilityClient.swift:699-775`). This prevents a late absolute deadline from being flattened into generic `failed`, `unverifiable`, or `securityRejected` before the validation caller can classify it.
- The shared checkpoint is cancellation-first and deadline-second: an attempt whose cancellation and deadline are both observable returns cancellation (`FeishuSpeech/Services/AccessibilityClient.swift:1594-1600`). `cancellationOr` retains the same precedence before selecting either the original security/identity failure or `accessibilityTimeout` (`FeishuSpeech/Services/AccessibilityClient.swift:1439-1446`).
- Every validation-critical AX helper receives the immutable absolute deadline and live cancellation probe. It checks before setting the per-element messaging timeout, immediately after that synchronous return, before the substantive AX operation, and immediately after the substantive return (`FeishuSpeech/Services/AccessibilityClient.swift:1613-1674`, `FeishuSpeech/Services/AccessibilityClient.swift:1690-1809`, `FeishuSpeech/Services/AccessibilityClient.swift:1811-1875`, `FeishuSpeech/Services/AccessibilityClient.swift:1967-2004`). Range decoding additionally checks before and after `AXValueGetValue`; selected-range creation checks after `AXValueCreate` and before the setter.
- The result-specific adapters no longer collapse `.deadline`: element, range, string, settable, PID, and mutation-operation adapters each return their corresponding typed deadline case (`FeishuSpeech/Services/AccessibilityClient.swift:1462-1592`). Consequently the nine R5 RED occurrences after exact focus copy, selected-range readback and decode, and role/subrole reads now propagate through `.deadline` rather than generic failure.
- Validation callers map every typed late deadline to `.accessibilityTimeout`: application PID and focused element (`FeishuSpeech/Services/AccessibilityClient.swift:845-905`, `FeishuSpeech/Services/AccessibilityClient.swift:1029-1066`), application-bound focus (`FeishuSpeech/Services/AccessibilityClient.swift:1070-1104`), exact restoration and readback (`FeishuSpeech/Services/AccessibilityClient.swift:1161-1312`), and exact editable/PID validation (`FeishuSpeech/Services/AccessibilityClient.swift:1315-1356`). A failure branch that must distinguish a deadline racing with a security or identity result uses `cancellationOr`, preserving cancellation precedence.
- Security classification remains fail closed. Malformed element/range/string values return typed failure or unverifiable; unexpected roles/subroles, secure text subrole, missing exact capabilities, and captured-element PID mismatch remain `securityRejected` rather than becoming timeout success (`FeishuSpeech/Services/AccessibilityClient.swift:1262-1356`, `FeishuSpeech/Services/AccessibilityClient.swift:1888-1950`, `FeishuSpeech/Services/AccessibilityClient.swift:1967-2004`). Secure Input, Accessibility trust, full identity, and frontmost drift remain independently rejected by both security composites (`FeishuSpeech/Services/AccessibilityClient.swift:1376-1436`).
- The application-bound exception is unchanged and narrow. Only focused-element `noValue` or `attributeUnsupported` becomes `AXElementRead.unavailable`; the captured application root then returns the provisional ordinary-miss success (`FeishuSpeech/Services/AccessibilityClient.swift:1075-1098`, `FeishuSpeech/Services/AccessibilityClient.swift:1637-1673`). If a concrete focused element exists, its PID and editable role/subrole are still validated; ordinary role/subrole capability miss alone is allowed, while secure or unverifiable state is rejected and deadline remains timeout (`FeishuSpeech/Services/AccessibilityClient.swift:1029-1066`). Every provisional application-bound success must still pass the trailing security composite before commit (`FeishuSpeech/Services/AccessibilityClient.swift:845-905`).

## Fixed exhaustive System AX matrix

- Production exposes exactly 15 value-only `ReviewAXStepID` cases (`FeishuSpeech/Services/AccessibilityClient.swift:51-84`). The test owns a separate hand-authored 15-entry inventory and verifies its count and uniqueness; `isAttributeSettable` is explicitly classified as capture-only, while every other production step must appear in exact or application-bound validation (`FeishuSpeechTests/FinalTextOutputSecurityTests.swift:744-793`, `FeishuSpeechTests/FinalTextOutputSecurityTests.swift:3354-3378`). Manual review confirms all current production cases match this fixed inventory.
- Exact and application-bound expected traces are literal ordered arrays, including both security composites and the late focus, range, AXValue, role, subrole, and final PID steps (`FeishuSpeechTests/FinalTextOutputSecurityTests.swift:3380-3433`). Before any scenarios are generated, a real successful System runtime trace must equal each complete fixed array exactly (`FeishuSpeechTests/FinalTextOutputSecurityTests.swift:795-842`). An early production failure therefore fails the oracle rather than shortening its coverage.
- Cancellation and deadline scenarios are generated only from those fixed arrays. Each occurrence must be observed, must return the exact typed failure, and must be the final recorded AX step (`FeishuSpeechTests/FinalTextOutputSecurityTests.swift:3155-3251`). Deadline injection blocks for 300 ms at the selected occurrence against a 150 ms absolute deadline (`FeishuSpeechTests/FinalTextOutputSecurityTests.swift:3672-3697`), making the post-return classification deterministic.
- The R5 RED receipt records the fixed matrix's original nine `.securityRejected` versus `.accessibilityTimeout` failures (`kaola-workflow/issue-40/test-green-v5.md:1129-1203`). The repaired production file was last modified at 18:01:08 +0800; the current fixed matrix then passed in both authoritative logs at 18:04 and 18:05 (`/tmp/issue40-v5-r5-focused-20260824.log:1900-1917`, `/tmp/issue40-v5-r5-full-20260824.log:2353-2370`). ## Previously closed security and privacy boundaries

- Immediate commit still runs the leading composite, fixed-binding validation, and trailing composite before the modifier and combined-epoch reservation. Pair construction/readback precedes commit and every reservation retry returns through current validation (`FeishuSpeech/Services/AccessibilityClient.swift:845-905`, `FeishuSpeech/Services/ReviewSubmissionExecutor.swift:946-1005`). No AX validation or callback occurs while the commit locks are held.
- The target remains the captured positive PID plus full bundle, executable URL, and launch-date identity. Exact validation retains the captured element and range; application-bound validation reads only the captured application object; both direct Unicode events retain the same immutable PID (`FeishuSpeech/Services/AccessibilityClient.swift:1029-1356`, `FeishuSpeech/Services/ReviewSubmissionExecutor.swift:438-500`). There is no ambient retarget or exact-to-application-bound downgrade at confirmation.
- Lifecycle monitoring still owns distinct opaque leases, fails closed if its activation/termination/process-generation/local/global observers are unavailable, and allows only the exact lease to retire its target. Physical and lifecycle observations advance the shared epoch without obtaining submission authority (`FeishuSpeech/Services/ReviewSubmissionExecutor.swift:1180-1326`, `FeishuSpeech/Services/ReviewSubmissionExecutor.swift:1433-1575`). Event exemptions continue to require both the private tag and this process PID.
- Admission retains the 16,384 UTF-16 cap. The prepared down/up pair carries exact UTF-16 code units, empty flags, the exact private tag, own source PID, and one immutable target PID, with all fields read back before commit (`FeishuSpeech/Services/ReviewSubmissionExecutor.swift:438-582`). Down remains the sole irreversible boundary; the matching up is attempted synchronously exactly once, and all post-boundary outcomes remain `submittedUnverified` with no retry or resend (`FeishuSpeech/Services/ReviewSubmissionExecutor.swift:1008-1048`).
- Confirmation intent remains fileprivate to the real Send-button and qualified panel-Return handlers. Return requires the exact key panel and window, main Return or keypad Enter, no repeat or disallowed modifier, an in-panel responder, nonblank content, and no marked-text composition (`FeishuSpeech/Controllers/ReviewWindowController.swift:11-91`, `FeishuSpeech/Controllers/ReviewWindowController.swift:669-704`). No test helper can directly mint the opaque gesture marker.
- The default application path constructs `SystemReviewSubmissionFacade` and leaves legacy destination delivery nil (`FeishuSpeech/ViewModels/MainViewModel.swift:343-377`). Real confirmation issues one opaque handle and one admission envelope only for the captured production target (`FeishuSpeech/ViewModels/MainViewModel.swift:2120-2210`). Current accepted-path scans found no pasteboard, Cmd+V, app activation, global Return confirmation, pre-confirm AX mutation, output retry, or transcript-content logging. The remaining activation method belongs only to the explicitly injected legacy compatibility delivery and cannot be selected by the default production composition.
- Recording and recognition remain separate asynchronous roots. No candidate diff exists in `AudioRecorder`, `FeishuStreamingSession`, `FeishuAPIService`, `HoldPacketJournal`, `ByteBoundedAudioIngress`, or `DirectFeishuKeepAliveSession`; MainViewModel still starts independent capture-drain and recognition-consumer tasks. Current `git diff --check` is clean.

review_conclusion: The repaired AX classifiers preserve exact deadline and cancellation authority across every validation-critical return, the fixed matrix cannot self-shrink, and no blocking security or privacy regression remains in the reviewed candidate.
